questions.question: What fundamentally distinguishes a VANET from a general MANET?

options.A: VANETs require internet access at all times
options.B: VANETs operate in vehicular environments with very high mobility, frequent topology changes, and safety-critical constraints
options.C: VANETs use only infrastructure-based communication
options.D: VANETs are static networks with fixed routing tables 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: In a VANET, if RSUs are removed entirely, which statement best describes the remaining network?

options.A: The network ceases to function
options.B: Vehicles can still communicate in pure V2V ad hoc mode using OBUs
options.C: Cellular coverage automatically replaces RSU functionality
options.D: Vehicles must wait for RSUs to be restored before communicating 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes CSMA/CA compared to CSMA/CD?

options.A: CSMA/CD is used in wireless networks; CSMA/CA is used in wired networks
options.B: CSMA/CA avoids collisions before transmission using backoff; CSMA/CD detects collisions after they occur
options.C: CSMA/CA is faster than CSMA/CD for vehicular use
options.D: CSMA/CD is preferred for DSRC because it has lower overhead 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: What is the primary reason multi-hop packet forwarding is essential in VANETs?

options.A: Single-hop transmission always reaches all vehicles
options.B: It extends communication range beyond a single node's direct radio reach without requiring infrastructure
options.C: It reduces the need for GNSS modules
options.D: It simplifies routing protocols by eliminating the need for certificates 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Which statement about OBU components is CORRECT?

options.A: The GNSS module controls braking
options.B: The security module is optional in modern OBUs
options.C: The V2X communication module handles both DSRC and C-V2X protocols
options.D: The antenna system is only used for cellular communication 6 Correct Answer: C

questions.question: A connected vehicle provides '360-degree situational awareness' ² what technology primarily enables this compared to automated vehicles?

options.A: Higher resolution cameras
options.B: V2X communication systems that share data from vehicles and infrastructure beyond sensor line- of-sight
options.C: Better LIDAR resolution
options.D: Faster in-vehicle processors 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Why does V2V communication detect driver intent (e.g., braking) more reliably than camera-based systems?

options.A: Cameras cannot detect color
options.B: BSMs transmit brake status, speed, and trajectory data directly ² information cameras can only infer indirectly
options.C: V2V has higher resolution than cameras
options.D: V2V operates at night while cameras do not 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Which property makes ad hoc networks 'self-configuring'?

options.A: They rely on a central server to assign IP addresses
options.B: Nodes discover each other and establish routing paths dynamically without pre-configuration
options.C: Network administrators configure them before deployment
options.D: They use static IP addresses assigned at manufacturing 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: In the V2X taxonomy, V2P communication is most critical for:

options.A: Reducing highway congestion
options.B: Warning pedestrians and cyclists of approaching vehicles at intersections or crossings
options.C: Providing cloud-based navigation updates
options.D: Enabling vehicle platooning on motorways 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: An RSU does NOT enforce a strict hierarchical structure. What does this mean for VANET operations?

options.A: RSUs are the primary control nodes of all V2X traffic
options.B: Vehicles remain autonomous and can communicate directly without RSU involvement, preserving the ad hoc nature
options.C: RSUs must authenticate every V2V message
options.D: VANETs cannot function without at least one RSU per kilometer 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: What is the main technical reason why V2V is categorized as 'platooning' (V2V use case)?

options.A: Platooning requires cellular connectivity through the Uu interface
options.B: Platooning requires direct real-time vehicle-to-vehicle exchange of speed, position, and braking data to maintain tight formation
options.C: Platooning works best with RSU coordination only
options.D: Platooning is a V2N application because it requires cloud coordination 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: What does 'peer-to-peer' communication in MANETs mean for routing responsibilities?

options.A: One designated master node handles all routing
options.B: Every node acts as both transmitter and router, forwarding packets on behalf of others
options.C: Only RSUs forward packets between vehicles
options.D: Peer-to-peer means direct one-hop communication only ² no forwarding 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Which of these is the most technically accurate reason RSUs are mounted with omnidirectional antennas?

options.A: To reduce interference between adjacent RSUs
options.B: To broadcast coverage equally in all 360° directions so vehicles approaching from any direction receive messages
options.C: To increase range beyond 5 km
options.D: Omnidirectional antennas are cheaper than directional ones 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: A mesh network node fails. Which behavior characterizes a self-healing mesh network?

options.A: The network stops working until the node is replaced
options.B: Traffic is automatically rerouted through alternative paths without human intervention
options.C: A central server assigns new paths to all nodes
options.D: Adjacent nodes must be manually reconfigured 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Which statement about the OBU GNSS module is most technically precise?

options.A: GNSS provides connectivity to cellular networks
options.B: GNSS provides precise vehicle position data included in BSMs for collision detection algorithms
options.C: GNSS manages V2X security certificates
options.D: GNSS communicates directly with RSUs to relay position data 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Why are BSMs broadcast 10 times per second specifically?

options.A: 10 Hz is the maximum rate supported by IEEE 802.11p
options.B: At typical highway speeds, 100ms intervals provide sufficient position update frequency for collision avoidance algorithms
options.C: 10 Hz matches the refresh rate of vehicle dashboards
options.D: The 5.9 GHz spectrum is partitioned into exactly 10 slots per second 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: What does 'dynamic topology' in MANETs/VANETs mean for routing protocols?

options.A: Routes are pre-computed and stored in each vehicle
options.B: Routes change frequently as vehicles move, requiring protocols that can discover and update paths on-the-fly
options.C: Topology is managed centrally by the TMC
options.D: Dynamic topology only applies to infrastructure-based networks 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Which factor makes VANETs more challenging than general MANETs from a network design perspective?

options.A: VANETs use more expensive hardware
options.B: Vehicles move much faster and more predictably (road-constrained) but with very short contact durations between nodes
options.C: VANETs require more frequency bands than MANETs
options.D: VANETs have smaller network sizes than MANETs 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: The 'no central infrastructure' property of ad hoc networks creates which specific challenge for VANETs?

options.A: Lack of GPS support
options.B: No centralized trust anchor for authentication ² requiring distributed security mechanisms like SCMS
options.C: Vehicles cannot use OFDM modulation
options.D: Channel access cannot be coordinated at all 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: If a vehicle with only an OBU (no RSU nearby) needs to warn a vehicle 800m ahead about a hazard, what must occur?

options.A: The warning cannot be sent as DSRC range is 300m
options.B: Multi-hop relaying ² intermediate vehicles forward the BSM extending the effective range
options.C: The vehicle must use cellular V2N to send the alert
options.D: No mechanism exists for this scenario in VANET design 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Why is V2I communication at tunnels particularly valuable compared to open roads?

options.A: Tunnels have better cellular coverage
options.B: Tunnels block line-of-sight for sensors and GPS signals, making infrastructure-provided ahead-of- curve warnings critical
options.C: RSUs in tunnels use higher power
options.D: V2V works better inside tunnels due to signal reflection 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: A connected vehicle receives a SPaT message. What does the vehicle do with this data?

options.A: It updates its infotainment map display
options.B: It uses signal phase and timing to optimize speed for green light passage or prepare to stop
options.C: It reports the data to the TMC for logging
options.D: It re-broadcasts the SPaT to nearby vehicles via V2V 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: What distinguishes a 'Connected Automated Vehicle' (CAV) from a standard 'Automated Vehicle' (AV)?

options.A: CAVs have more sensors than AVs
options.B: CAVs combine internal sensing (automation) with external V2X communication for information beyond sensor range
options.C: AVs use cellular networks while CAVs use DSRC
options.D: CAVs do not require any internal sensors 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: BSMs are broadcast without acknowledgment. What does this 'broadcast-only' nature imply for system design?

options.A: Every vehicle must confirm receipt of each BSM
options.B: Safety applications must tolerate occasional packet loss and use redundant periodic transmission to compensate
options.C: BSMs are encrypted point-to-point to the nearest RSU
options.D: TCP is used to guarantee delivery of each BSM 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Why is cooperative mapping preferable to individual vehicle mapping for localization accuracy?

options.A: Individual vehicles have more processing power
options.B: Multiple vehicles contribute overlapping sensor data from different angles, reducing cumulative localization error
options.C: Cooperative maps use satellite data only
options.D: Individual mapping is more accurate because it avoids data conflicts 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: In a V2I system, what is the functional difference between a TMC and an RSU?

options.A: TMC is a physical roadside device; RSU is a remote data center
options.B: RSU handles local wireless V2X communication; TMC is a centralized system coordinating traffic management using remote communications
options.C: TMC broadcasts safety messages; RSU manages cellular handover
options.D: Both perform identical functions at different geographic scales 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Which scenario demonstrates the limitations of radar compared to V2V communication?

options.A: Detecting a vehicle directly in front at 10m
options.B: Detecting brake lights of a vehicle two cars ahead blocked by a truck (non-line-of-sight)
options.C: Measuring precise vehicle speed
options.D: Detecting lane markings on wet roads 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: A V2I system uses PSID (Provider Service Identifier). What is the technical purpose of PSID?

options.A: It identifies the vehicle's license plate over V2X
options.B: It identifies which application a V2X message belongs to, allowing devices to filter relevant messages
options.C: It encrypts the V2I message payload
options.D: It assigns a radio channel for the V2I communication 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Connectivity extends the sensing range of vehicles. What specific technical mechanism enables this?

options.A: Better antenna gain
options.B: Vehicles share their sensor perceptions (position, speed, hazard data) via V2X, creating a collective sensing range larger than any individual sensor
options.C: RSUs amplify radar signals from vehicles
options.D: Cellular networks relay sensor data between vehicles 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: In rural overtaking scenarios (passing on rural roads), why is V2V specifically more valuable than radar?

options.A: Radar is illegal on rural roads
options.B: Oncoming vehicles beyond the visual horizon can proactively share position/speed via BSM, while radar requires line-of-sight
options.C: V2V operates at longer range frequencies on rural roads
options.D: Rural roads have more RSUs than urban roads 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: What is the technical significance of OBU processing BSMs '10 times per second' for safety applications?

options.A: It matches the GPS update rate of 10 Hz
options.B: At 100km/h, a vehicle travels 2.8m per 100ms ² frequent updates are needed to maintain accurate neighboring vehicle models for collision assessment
options.C: 10 Hz matches the human reaction time threshold
options.D: IEEE 1609.3 mandates exactly 10 Hz for all V2X messages 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: A connected vehicle loses RSU connectivity temporarily. Which statement is MOST accurate?

options.A: All safety functions cease immediately
options.B: V2V communication continues unaffected ² V2I loss degrades infrastructure-based services but not peer-to-peer safety messaging
options.C: The vehicle automatically switches to satellite
options.D: BSM transmission automatically stops without RSU coverage 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: What does 'infrastructure sensing' provide that individual vehicle sensing cannot?

options.A: Better camera resolution
options.B: A fixed elevated vantage point that can monitor traffic without being blocked by other vehicles, providing persistent coverage
options.C: Lower latency than in-vehicle sensors
options.D: Longer range radar than OBU-mounted systems 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: The display panel in a connected vehicle receives an alert. What determines whether the alert is shown or acted upon automatically?

options.A: The RSU decides which alerts to show
options.B: The OBU application layer evaluates threat severity and context to determine whether to warn the driver or trigger an automated response
options.C: The TMC sends display instructions to each vehicle individually
options.D: All received BSMs trigger dashboard alerts automatically 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Why does removing traffic lights at intersections become feasible with V2I connected infrastructure?

options.A: Cameras on RSUs replace signal timing
options.B: Vehicles can communicate position and intent via V2X, allowing real-time cooperative negotiation of intersection passage without fixed signal phases
options.C: RSUs replace physical traffic lights with audio signals
options.D: Connected vehicles simply ignore traffic lights 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: What does 'path history' in a BSM enable receiving vehicles to calculate?

options.A: The sender vehicle's fuel consumption
options.B: A trajectory prediction of the sending vehicle's future path for proactive collision threat assessment
options.C: The insurance status of the sending vehicle
options.D: The sending vehicle's destination for routing purposes 6 Correct Answer: B

options.C: Two-way transactions require cellular networks, not DSRC

questions.question: How does V2X connectivity help vehicles 'with different automation levels' interact?

options.A: Highly automated vehicles override lower-automation ones
options.B: V2X provides a common communication layer ² a fully automated vehicle can receive intent/position from a manually driven vehicle that has an OBU
options.C: Automation level is automatically detected by RSUs

questions.question: In V2I, what is the purpose of 'Vehicle Data' (latitude, longitude, speed, brake status) sent TO infrastructure?

options.A: The TMC uses it to control the vehicle remotely
options.B: Infrastructure aggregates vehicle probe data to monitor traffic conditions and improve dynamic signal timing and hazard detection

options.D: Vehicle data is stored in OBU memory only and never transmitted 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Which metric is MOST directly linked to V2I system effectiveness at preventing intersection crashes?

options.A: Total number of RSUs deployed
options.B: End-to-end latency of SPaT and MAP messages ² lower latency means vehicles receive signal timing in time to adjust speed appropriately

options.D: Number of vehicles with infotainment displays 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: DSRC uses IEEE 802.11p (not standard Wi-Fi). What specific modification makes 802.11p suitable for vehicular use?

options.A: It uses a different frequency band
options.B: It eliminates the association/handshake process enabling immediate one-way broadcast ² critical for vehicles passing at high speed
options.C: It increases channel bandwidth to 40 MHz
options.D: It adds TCP reliability to DSRC transmissions 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: The DSRC protocol stack places WSMP alongside IP/UDP. What does this architectural choice enable?

options.A: WSMP provides a backup path if IP fails
options.B: Safety-critical BSMs bypass the heavier IP stack via WSMP for lower latency, while non-safety apps use IP/UDP
options.C: WSMP encrypts IP packets before transmission
options.D: WSMP is only used for RSU-to-TMC communication 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: IEEE 1609.4 defines multi-channel operation. What specific problem does this solve in DSRC?

options.A: It eliminates the need for a control channel
options.B: It allows devices to alternate between the control channel (safety) and service channels (non-safety), preventing safety messages from being displaced by non-safety traffic
options.C: It allows all 7 channels to be used simultaneously
options.D: It solves the hidden node problem in dense deployments 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: DSRC uses OFDM modulation. Why is OFDM specifically chosen over simpler modulations for vehicular channels?

options.A: OFDM requires less processing power
options.B: OFDM is robust against multipath fading and Doppler spread caused by fast-moving vehicles ² sub-carriers spread the signal across frequency
options.C: OFDM provides higher power output
options.D: OFDM eliminates the need for error correction codes 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: The DSRC control channel (CH 178) is separated from service channels. Why must safety messages ONLY use the control channel?

options.A: Service channels do not support BSM format
options.B: Guaranteed airtime on the control channel ensures safety messages are not delayed by competing non-safety service channel traffic
options.C: The control channel has higher transmit power
options.D: Service channels are encrypted and cannot carry unencrypted BSMs 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: DSRC has a 10 MHz channel bandwidth ² half of standard Wi-Fi (20 MHz). What is the technical consequence?

options.A: DSRC has twice the data rate of Wi-Fi
options.B: Lower bandwidth means lower data rate but better coverage and robustness in high-mobility, high- Doppler vehicular environments
options.C: DSRC cannot carry safety messages due to low bandwidth
options.D: 10 MHz allows DSRC to operate at longer range than Wi-Fi 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: IEEE 1609.2 handles security in DSRC. What specific security service does it provide for BSMs?

options.A: End-to-end encryption of BSM payload
options.B: Digital signatures using pseudonym certificates to authenticate the message sender without revealing permanent identity
options.C: Firewall functions for RSU-to-vehicle communication
options.D: Symmetric key encryption for all V2V messages 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: DSRC operates in the 5.9 GHz band. What regulatory reason specifically reserves this spectrum for V2X?

options.A: 5.9 GHz provides the best range for vehicular communication
options.B: The 75 MHz allocation (5.850±5.925 GHz) was specifically licensed for safety-critical ITS use, isolating it from general consumer Wi-Fi interference
options.C: 5.9 GHz is cheaper to license than other bands
options.D: 5.9 GHz was chosen because it has no existing users 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: WSMP (WAVE Short Message Protocol) is used instead of TCP for safety messages. Why is TCP unsuitable for V2V safety messaging?

options.A: TCP requires more bandwidth than DSRC can provide
options.B: TCP's handshake, acknowledgment, and retransmission overhead add latency incompatible with sub-50ms safety alert requirements
options.C: TCP cannot operate in the 5.9 GHz band
options.D: TCP is not supported in IEEE 802.11p at all 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: CSMA/CA is the MAC layer for DSRC. What specific mechanism does CSMA/CA use to reduce collision probability?

options.A: It detects collisions after they occur and retransmits immediately
options.B: Each node listens for channel activity and, if busy, waits a random backoff period before attempting transmission
options.C: CSMA/CA uses time slots assigned by an RSU
options.D: CSMA/CA prioritizes messages by vehicle speed 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: WAVE Service Advertisement (WSA) is defined in IEEE 1609.3. What is its function?

options.A: It advertises available road services to drivers via dashboard display
options.B: It allows service providers to announce available services and parameters, enabling devices to discover and join service channels
options.C: It is a security advertisement broadcast by SCMS
options.D: WSA is used only for toll payment services 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: The DSRC spectrum allocates CH 172 and CH 184 as 'Service channels (safety only)'. What distinguishes these from regular service channels?

options.A: They operate at higher power
options.B: They are reserved for safety-only service communications, not general non-safety applications, maintaining safety message prioritization
options.C: They use a different modulation scheme
options.D: They are shared with DSRC's control channel 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Why does DSRC specify a maximum of 10 MHz per channel rather than using wider channels?

options.A: Wider channels are not supported by IEEE 802.11
options.B: Narrower channels improve robustness under Doppler shift at high vehicle speeds and allow more channels within the 75 MHz allocation
options.C: 10 MHz provides the highest data rate for V2X
options.D: Regulatory bodies mandated 10 MHz before the standard was written 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'Reserved 5 MHz' at the bottom of the DSRC band?

options.A: It is used for RSU-to-TMC backhaul
options.B: It acts as a guard band to prevent interference with adjacent spectrum allocations below 5.850 GHz
options.C: It is reserved for future 5G deployment
options.D: Emergency vehicles use this 5 MHz exclusively 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: DSRC authentication uses pseudonym certificates that change frequently. Why would a vehicle using the SAME certificate for months create a problem?

options.A: Certificates expire after 30 days regardless
options.B: A stable long-term identifier allows observers to link all messages to one vehicle, enabling tracking and privacy violation
options.C: Long-lived certificates are computationally expensive to verify
options.D: The SCMS mandates certificate changes for billing purposes 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: In DSRC, what happens when a vehicle moves out of RSU coverage but continues driving?

options.A: All V2X communication stops
options.B: The vehicle continues V2V communication via PC5 ² RSU is only needed for V2I services, not V2V safety messages
options.C: The vehicle automatically switches to 4G LTE for V2V
options.D: The OBU enters sleep mode to conserve power 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: IEEE 1609.4 requires devices to switch between CCH and SCH in interleaved intervals. What latency concern does this create?

options.A: It eliminates all latency for safety messages
options.B: If a BSM arrives during a SCH interval, it must wait until the next CCH interval ² potentially adding 50ms+ delay
options.C: Channel switching takes 0ms in 802.11p hardware
options.D: Safety messages always interrupt SCH to avoid delay 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: DSRC's BSM is broadcast without acknowledgment. Which design principle justifies this decision?

options.A: Acknowledgment reduces latency
options.B: In V2V safety messaging, the overhead of unicast acknowledgment from hundreds of neighbors would overwhelm the channel ² reliable delivery relies on high-frequency repetition instead
options.C: IEEE 802.11p does not support acknowledgment frames
options.D: Acknowledgment is handled by the application layer in DSRC 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: The DSRC standard separates IEEE 802.11p (PHY/MAC) from IEEE 1609.x (upper layers). What architectural benefit does this separation provide?

options.A: It allows different modulation schemes per 1609.x standard
options.B: It modularizes the stack ² upper-layer protocols (security, networking, applications) can evolve independently without changing the radio hardware
options.C: It reduces the cost of OBU manufacturing
options.D: Separation forces all V2X to use the same frequency 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Why is DSRC described as having 'limited scalability in dense environments' despite using CSMA/CA?

options.A: Dense environments have too many RSUs
options.B: As vehicle density increases, more nodes compete for the shared channel simultaneously, increasing collision probability and channel load despite CSMA/CA's backoff mechanism
options.C: DSRC uses a fixed number of time slots that cannot scale
options.D: Dense environments cause GNSS interference with DSRC 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Why is 'Packet Reception Ratio' (PRR) a more meaningful metric than throughput for evaluating DSRC safety systems?

options.A: PRR is easier to measure than throughput
options.B: Safety depends on what fraction of transmitted safety messages are successfully received ² a high throughput system with low PRR may still fail to prevent collisions
options.C: Throughput cannot be measured in broadcast systems
options.D: PRR is mandated by IEEE standards while throughput is not 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: At 250 km/h, two vehicles approach each other head-on. What specific DSRC design challenge does this extreme speed create?

options.A: Channel bandwidth is insufficient
options.B: Doppler spread is very high, degrading OFDM subcarrier orthogonality ² requiring specific Doppler compensation in the PHY layer
options.C: BSMs cannot be transmitted at vehicle speeds above 200 km/h
options.D: GPS accuracy degrades at speeds above 200 km/h 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Hidden node' scenarios reduce DSRC reliability. What is the specific mechanism of failure?

options.A: RSUs block line-of-sight between vehicles
options.B: Vehicle A and Vehicle C cannot detect each other's transmissions but both transmit to Vehicle B simultaneously, causing a collision at B that neither A nor C detects
options.C: GNSS errors cause incorrect position reporting
options.D: Encryption overhead delays transmission enough to cause timing collisions 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Adaptive message rate control (like LIMERIC) reduces channel load. What unintended consequence must system designers consider?

options.A: Lower message rate increases encryption overhead
options.B: Reducing beacon rate in high-density scenarios means position updates are less frequent, potentially degrading tracking accuracy for fast-moving vehicles
options.C: Adaptive rate control increases RSU processing load
options.D: Lower message rates reduce GPS power consumption 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: DSRC channel congestion is specifically problematic because:

options.A: Congestion causes RSUs to shut down
options.B: High channel load degrades exactly the safety messages that high-traffic (high-density) scenarios most urgently require ² congestion peaks when safety is most critical
options.C: Congestion only affects non-safety service channels
options.D: Congestion increases latency for cellular V2N services 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Why is the 5.9 GHz sharing with Wi-Fi a technically complex problem beyond simple interference?

options.A: Wi-Fi uses more power than DSRC
options.B: Wi-Fi devices use aggressive CSMA/CA without DSRC-specific prioritization, potentially disrupting safety messages and fragmenting the band if DSRC and Wi-Fi must coexist
options.C: 5.9 GHz Wi-Fi is illegal in all V2X deployment regions
options.D: Wi-Fi and DSRC use different modulation schemes incompatible at the physical layer 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: What is the technical root cause of the 'service channel switching delay' problem in DSRC?

options.A: RSUs do not synchronize their channel switching
options.B: IEEE 1609.4 mandates alternating CCH and SCH intervals ² if a safety event occurs during an SCH interval, the BSM must wait until the next CCH interval to be transmitted
options.C: The OBU hardware requires 10ms to physically change frequency
options.D: Service channel switching only affects non-safety applications 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: In DSRC, why is 'adaptive transmit power control' an alternative (or complement) to message rate control for congestion management?

options.A: Higher power increases range and helps dense networks
options.B: Reducing transmit power limits the radio range ² fewer vehicles 'hear' each transmission, reducing contention on the shared channel
options.C: Adaptive power control is mandated by IEEE 1609.2
options.D: Power control increases PRR by boosting signal strength 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: DSRC requires low-latency communication. Which latency budget breakdown is most technically accurate for a V2V safety alert?

options.A: All latency is from propagation delay
options.B: Total latency includes: channel access wait time (CSMA/CA backoff) + transmission time + processing time ² backoff can dominate under congestion
options.C: Latency is fixed at exactly 50ms by IEEE 802.11p
options.D: Latency only matters for V2I applications, not V2V 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Why is 'line-of-sight (LOS)' degradation in urban environments a fundamental DSRC challenge rather than a simple engineering problem?

options.A: Urban buildings reflect signals, improving range
options.B: Buildings, trucks, and obstacles create non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions that introduce multipath fading and can block safety-critical messages at the exact locations (intersections) where they are most needed
options.C: Urban environments have better RSU coverage to compensate
options.D: DSRC antennas in urban environments can be raised to overcome building blockage 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: What specific technical problem does 'message filtering and prioritization' solve in dense DSRC networks?

options.A: It reduces the number of RSUs needed
options.B: It selectively forwards only the most relevant messages (e.g., nearby vehicles) and assigns higher priority to safety vs non-safety, reducing effective channel load without reducing safety message delivery
options.C: Message filtering is applied at the RSU level only
options.D: Prioritization ensures all 7 DSRC channels are used equally 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: PRR decreases with increasing vehicle density even with CSMA/CA. Why does CSMA/CA fail to fully protect PRR?

options.A: CSMA/CA cannot detect transmissions from more than 5 neighbors
options.B: As density grows, backoff periods become insufficient ² multiple nodes simultaneously exit backoff and transmit, causing collisions that CSMA/CA cannot prevent (only reduce)
options.C: CSMA/CA was not designed for vehicular environments
options.D: High density causes GNSS errors that corrupt BSMs 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Timing synchronization' is important in DSRC. What specific failure occurs without precise time synchronization?

options.A: GPS position data becomes inaccurate
options.B: CCH/SCH channel switching in IEEE 1609.4 requires synchronized timeslots across all devices ² without sync, devices switch channels at different times and miss messages from neighbors
options.C: BSM transmission rate drops below 10 Hz
options.D: Security certificates cannot be validated without synchronized clocks 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: DSRC prioritizes safety messaging over high bandwidth. What specifically is sacrificed to achieve low latency?

options.A: Message range is reduced
options.B: Data rate is limited (3±27 Mbps) and channel bandwidth is narrow (10 MHz) to optimize for robustness and low latency at the cost of throughput
options.C: Security services are disabled
options.D: V2I communication is disabled in safety priority mode 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: A DSRC system with high PRR but high latency would still fail safety requirements. Why?

options.A: High latency means RSUs reject the message
options.B: A collision warning received 300ms after the collision trigger point provides insufficient time for driver response or automated braking ² timing and reliability must both be met
options.C: High latency automatically reduces PRR

questions.question: Release 16 focuses on 'teleoperated driving.' What does this use case require from the sidelink that no previous V2X generation could provide?

options.B: Ultra-reliable bidirectional real-time link: the remote operator needs <10ms round-trip control commands (downlink) AND real-time high-quality video from the vehicle (uplink) ² NR-V2X URLLC provides this while LTE-V2X cannot
options.C: Satellite communication support
options.D: No special sidelink requirement ² teleoperation uses Uu only 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: In NR-V2X, 'resource allocation' involves both Mode 1 (network scheduled) and Mode 2 (autonomous). When would a fleet operator choose Mode 1 over Mode 2?

options.A: Mode 1 is always preferred in dense environments
options.B: Mode 1 is optimal when vehicles are in cellular coverage and coordinated resource management by the gNB can reduce inter-vehicle interference ² especially for vehicles in a managed fleet with predictable communication patterns
options.C: Mode 1 is the only option for emergency vehicles
options.D: Mode 1 is chosen when vehicles move faster than 100 km/h 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Cooperative maneuvering messages' in NR-V2X differ from BSMs. What do they contain that BSMs do not?

options.A: Vehicle identification numbers
options.B: Intended future trajectory, planned maneuver (e.g., lane change in 2 seconds), and coordination requests ² enabling neighboring vehicles to proactively adjust their behavior to accommodate the intended action
options.C: Engine status and fuel level
options.D: Insurance and registration information 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: UCNC (User-Centric No Cell Edge) solves what specific problem that traditional cellular handover cannot?

options.A: UCNC eliminates the need for base stations
options.B: Traditional handover creates coverage gaps and latency spikes at cell edges ² UCNC creates virtual/hyper cells where vehicles are simultaneously served by multiple gNBs, eliminating cell-edge boundaries
options.C: UCNC reduces the number of cells needed
options.D: UCNC is only relevant for pedestrians, not vehicles 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Massive MIMO uses many antennas simultaneously. What specific 5G-V2X challenge does this address?

options.A: Massive MIMO increases the number of V2X channels
options.B: Massive MIMO enables spatial multiplexing ² different vehicles in the same frequency-time resource can be separated using beam steering, dramatically increasing system capacity without additional spectrum
options.C: Massive MIMO reduces OBU manufacturing cost
options.D: Massive MIMO increases the range of PC5 direct links 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: mmWave frequencies (>24 GHz) provide high bandwidth but face specific challenges for vehicular use. Which challenge is most fundamental?

options.A: mmWave cannot support OFDM modulation
options.B: mmWave has very short propagation range and is highly susceptible to blockage by buildings, trucks, and even rain ² requiring precise beam alignment that is extremely challenging at vehicular speeds
options.C: mmWave is too expensive for vehicle deployment
options.D: mmWave frequencies are reserved for military use only 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Network slicing creates 'dedicated QoS behavior' for safety traffic. Without slicing, what specific failure mode can occur?

options.A: Safety messages are automatically prioritized regardless
options.B: A burst of infotainment traffic could temporarily consume network resources intended for safety messages, causing safety message delay ² slicing guarantees isolated resource allocation
options.C: Network capacity is always sufficient without slicing
options.D: Safety message traffic is always smaller than infotainment traffic 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Dual connectivity allows simultaneous LTE and 5G connections. For V2X specifically, what does this enable?

options.A: Vehicles can use two frequencies simultaneously for higher speed
options.B: During 5G coverage gaps, LTE provides seamless fallback ² vehicles maintain V2N connectivity and Uu-based services without interruption, ensuring service continuity during the transition period
options.C: Dual connectivity halves the latency of each interface
options.D: Dual connectivity is only used for infotainment streaming 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: MEC processes data 'close to the vehicle.' What specifically is meant by 'close to' and why does distance matter?

options.A: MEC is installed inside vehicles
options.B: MEC servers are co-located with or near base stations ² the key is reducing the geographic distance data must travel, since speed-of-light propagation over long distances contributes significantly to round-trip latency
options.C: MEC is located in the RSU hardware
options.D: Distance matters only for security, not latency 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: The SMF in the 5G core 'supports multicast and QoS control.' In the context of V2X multicast delivery, what role does SMF play?

options.A: SMF transmits the multicast packets to vehicles
options.B: SMF establishes and manages the multicast session ² assigning appropriate QoS parameters, selecting transmission paths, and coordinating between the gNB and UPF for efficient one-to-many delivery
options.C: SMF handles security certificate validation for multicast
options.D: SMF is a radio frequency management function 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Beamforming 'directs energy toward the intended receiver.' For fast-moving vehicles, what additional capability must the beamforming system have?

options.A: Higher transmit power for moving targets
options.B: Beam tracking ² the beam must continuously follow the moving vehicle, requiring real-time angle estimation and beam steering updates faster than the vehicle moves out of the beam footprint
options.C: Beamforming is static once configured for a route
options.D: Moving vehicles automatically return to broadcast mode 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Unified QoS across NR-Uu and NR-PC5' solves what specific interoperability problem?

options.A: It reduces the number of certificates needed
options.B: A vehicle switching between PC5 direct communication and Uu cellular communication needs consistent QoS treatment ² without unified QoS, the switch could cause service degradation or priority loss for safety messages
options.C: Unified QoS eliminates the need for network slicing
options.D: It allows PC5 and Uu to share the same physical frequency 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: MEC is described as critical for 'cooperative perception.' What would happen without MEC at intersections with 100+ vehicles sharing sensor data?

options.A: Sensor data would be sent to the cloud without issue
options.B: Without edge processing, all sensor data from 100 vehicles would travel to the distant cloud for aggregation ² the round-trip latency (100-300ms) would make the processed collective perception outdated by the time it returns
options.C: Vehicles would stop sharing sensor data automatically
options.D: RSUs would buffer all sensor data locally without processing 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: URLLC's 99.999% reliability target corresponds to what maximum failure rate?

options.A: 1 failure per 1,000 transmissions
options.B: 1 failure per 100,000 transmissions ² in a V2X system with 10 safety messages per second, this means approximately 1 message failure per ~2.8 hours per vehicle
options.C: 1 failure per 1 million transmissions
options.D: 0 failures ² URLLC means perfect reliability 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Virtual cell' architecture creates a 'seamless wide-area service region.' How does this specifically differ from UCNC's 'hyper cell'?

options.A: Virtual cells are smaller than hyper cells
options.B: A virtual cell serves an individual vehicle from the most suitable gNB(s) ² it's vehicle-centric. A hyper cell is the aggregated coverage region formed by multiple cells ² it's infrastructure-centric. Together they eliminate edge effects
options.C: Virtual cells are only used indoors; hyper cells outdoors
options.D: Virtual and hyper cells are identical ² just different names 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: In NR-PC5, 'multicast and unicast support' was a major advancement over LTE-PC5. What technical requirement of the link does unicast with HARQ feedback introduce?

options.A: Higher transmit power
options.B: A feedback channel from the receiver to confirm (ACK) or request retransmission (NACK) ² this requires knowing the target receiver's identity and establishing a unicast link, fundamentally changing PC5 from anonymous broadcast to addressed communication
options.C: A dedicated SCMS certificate for unicast links
options.D: Unicast over PC5 requires RSU relay 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Critical safety messages receive highest QoS priority' in the NR-Uu model. What happens at the gNB when both infotainment and safety messages queue simultaneously?

options.A: Messages are served in arrival order (FIFO)
options.B: The gNB's scheduler prioritizes the safety message for immediate transmission in the next available scheduling opportunity, potentially preempting or delaying the infotainment message ² this is the function of QoS priority classes
options.C: Safety and infotainment messages are transmitted simultaneously on different channels
options.D: The OBU decides which message to send first, not the gNB 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Beamforming and Massive MIMO are described as 'improving wireless throughput and reliability' together. Why are they more powerful combined than individually?

options.A: They operate at different frequencies, eliminating interference
options.B: Massive MIMO provides spatial multiplexing (multiple simultaneous links) while beamforming focuses energy directionally ² combined, they enable multiple high-SNR directional links simultaneously, multiplying both throughput and reliability
options.C: They use different security certificates, enabling parallel transmissions
options.D: Combined, they reduce transmission power requirements 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 5G enhancement technology 'flexible scheduling' is specifically valuable for V2X because vehicular traffic is:

options.A: Always periodic and predictable
options.B: Highly variable ² dense intersections alternate with sparse highways; flexible dynamic scheduling adapts resource allocation to instantaneous demand rather than worst-case static allocation
options.C: Exclusively non-safety infotainment
options.D: Bounded by DSRC channel allocation 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Why is mmWave 'challenging for vehicular communication' specifically due to 'beam alignment'?

options.A: mmWave beams are too wide to focus
options.B: At 200km/h, a vehicle's angular position relative to a base station changes rapidly ² maintaining a narrow mmWave beam precisely aligned with a fast-moving vehicle requires continuous real-time beam tracking with sub-millisecond update rates
options.C: Beam alignment requires satellite GPS not available in cities
options.D: mmWave beam alignment is only needed for fixed RSUs 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Network slicing provides 'separate QoS behavior for safety and infotainment traffic.' What would happen in an unsliced network during a traffic accident?

options.A: Safety messages would automatically preempt infotainment traffic
options.B: A surge of accident-related V2X safety messages could compete with ongoing infotainment traffic in the same unsliced network pool ² without isolation guarantees, safety message delivery would depend on whatever resources remain after general traffic
options.C: Unsliced networks always give safety messages priority
options.D: Infotainment traffic automatically pauses during accidents 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: MEC 'reduces reliance on central cloud servers.' For V2X cooperative perception specifically, why is central cloud reliance problematic even with high bandwidth?

options.A: Cloud servers cannot process V2X data
options.B: Round-trip propagation to a distant cloud server introduces 50-300ms latency ² by the time processed collective perception returns to vehicles, moving objects may have changed position by several meters, making the data too stale for safety decisions
options.C: Central cloud servers are too expensive for V2X use
options.D: Cloud servers cannot handle the encryption of V2X sensor data 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: UCNC's 'dual connectivity' means a vehicle connects to multiple gNBs simultaneously. What specific V2X benefit does this provide during handover?

options.A: Dual connectivity doubles the data rate
options.B: The vehicle maintains a connection to both the old and new gNB during handover ² safety-critical V2X sessions are maintained without interruption, eliminating the brief disconnection that single- connection handover creates
options.C: Dual connectivity is required for URLLC by 3GPP standard
options.D: Dual connectivity is only used for infotainment during handover 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Sidelink-based positioning' is useful when GNSS is degraded. What specific technical mechanism does PC5 sidelink use for positioning?

options.A: PC5 sidelink accesses GNSS satellites directly
options.B: Vehicles measure signal time-of-arrival, round-trip time, or angle-of-arrival from neighboring UEs' sidelink signals to estimate relative distances and positions ² creating a local positioning network independent of satellites
options.C: RSUs provide positioning signals when GNSS fails
options.D: Sidelink positioning uses cellular tower triangulation 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Why must new vehicles support BOTH LTE-V2X and 5G-V2X (dual mode)?

options.A: Regulatory bodies mandate both modes
options.B: During the transition period, the vehicle fleet will contain both legacy LTE-V2X vehicles and newer 5G-V2X vehicles ² dual-mode vehicles can communicate with both, maintaining safety in mixed fleets
options.C: Dual mode is required only for platooning applications
options.D: 5G-V2X alone is sufficient once deployed in an area 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: MEC at intersections specifically enables 'real-time signal coordination and collision avoidance.' What data does the intersection MEC process that individual vehicles cannot?

options.A: Satellite GPS signals for all vehicles
options.B: Data from ALL vehicles approaching the intersection simultaneously ² individual vehicles only see their own trajectory, while MEC aggregates all trajectories to detect conflict points no individual vehicle can predict
options.C: Traffic light timing from the TMC
options.D: Historical accident data for the intersection 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Relay-capable UE operation' extends coverage for out-of-coverage vehicles. What specific technical challenge does the relay UE face?

options.A: The relay UE must switch to satellite communication
options.B: The relay UE must simultaneously maintain a direct PC5 link to the out-of-coverage vehicle AND a Uu link to the cellular network ² requiring radio resource management for two simultaneous half- duplex links on potentially the same or different channels
options.C: Relay UEs automatically increase transmit power
options.D: Relay UEs require a special license from the operator 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Tunnel scenarios: 'PC5 direct links' are preferred. What happens to Uu-based V2N services in a long tunnel?

options.A: Uu performance improves inside tunnels due to waveguide effect
options.B: Cellular signal typically degrades or disappears in long tunnels without embedded antennas ² V2N services become unavailable, but PC5 V2V communication continues between vehicles in the tunnel without infrastructure
options.C: Tunnels always have RSUs that maintain Uu connectivity
options.D: Vehicles automatically switch to Wi-Fi inside tunnels 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Full IoV ecosystem deployment' is the final deployment roadmap phase. What distinguishes this from initial C-V2X deployment?

options.A: IoV uses different hardware than C-V2X
options.B: Full IoV ecosystem integrates V2X with cloud services, AI analytics, smart city infrastructure, and diverse mobility platforms ² not just vehicle-to-vehicle safety messaging but a comprehensive intelligent transportation system
options.C: IoV deployment eliminates RSUs entirely
options.D: Full IoV is defined as 100% vehicle penetration rate 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'V2X T-Box acts as a central communication gateway.' What does this mean architecturally?

options.A: T-Box replaces OBU in modern vehicles
options.B: The T-Box aggregates in-vehicle network data (CAN bus, sensors) and manages external V2X communication interfaces (PC5, Uu, Wi-Fi), acting as the single integration point between internal vehicle systems and external V2X networks
options.C: T-Box is a cloud server not installed in vehicles
options.D: T-Box only handles security certificate management 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Combining NR-Uu and NR-PC5 provides 'complementary reliability and latency improvements.' What is the specific failure mode that each interface protects against?

options.A: Both interfaces protect against the same failure modes
options.B: PC5 protects against cellular outages (direct local communication works without infrastructure); Uu protects against PC5 range limitations and provides wide-area services ² failures in one interface are compensated by the other
options.C: Uu protects against packet loss; PC5 protects against latency
options.D: PC5 protects against security attacks; Uu protects against congestion 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'RSU/MEC-assisted V2X deployment' is described as best for intersection coordination. What specific technical advantage does RSU-mounted MEC have over cloud-based processing?

options.A: RSU MEC has more processing power than cloud servers
options.B: RSU-mounted MEC processes vehicle data locally at the intersection ² eliminating the round-trip to a remote cloud server and providing sub-10ms response time for safety coordination impossible with cloud latency
options.C: RSU MEC eliminates the need for V2X certificates
options.D: RSU MEC enables encryption not available in cloud 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Uu-based deployment challenge: latency and broadcasting limitations.' What specific broadcasting limitation does Uu have compared to PC5?

options.A: Uu cannot transmit more than 1 Mbps
options.B: Uu requires messages to go through the cellular network infrastructure ² true one-to-all local broadcast (as in PC5) is not native to Uu; achieving broadcast-like V2X safety messaging via Uu requires multicast groups or individual unicasts, adding complexity and latency
options.C: Uu broadcasting is limited to 100m range
options.D: Uu cannot carry BSM-formatted messages 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: The RSU dual interface 'Uu + PC5' allows what specific capability that single-interface RSUs cannot provide?

options.A: Higher transmit power in both directions
options.B: The RSU can receive direct PC5 V2I messages from nearby vehicles AND forward relevant data to the cellular network via Uu ² bridging local V2X communication to wide-area infrastructure services like TMC coordination
options.C: Dual interface eliminates the need for security certificates
options.D: Single-interface RSUs can perform all functions using software upgrades 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Lack of continuous coverage' is a 5G-Uu deployment limitation. For safety-critical V2X, what architectural solution addresses this gap?

options.A: Vehicles wait until coverage is restored
options.B: PC5 direct communication provides a coverage-independent safety fallback ² when Uu is unavailable, V2V safety messages continue via PC5, ensuring safety communication persists in coverage gaps
options.C: Satellite backhaul fills all coverage gaps
options.D: Safety messages are cached and sent when coverage is restored 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'PC5-based deployment is ideal for forward collision warning.' Why specifically is PC5 better than Uu for this application?

options.A: PC5 has higher bandwidth for collision data
options.B: Forward collision warning requires sub-100ms end-to-end latency ² Uu's network round-trip adds 30-100ms, while PC5's direct link achieves 1-5ms, providing 10-20x more reaction time in the critical pre-collision window
options.C: Uu does not support collision warning messages
options.D: PC5 encryption is stronger for safety-critical data 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Remote driving and platooning benefit most from MEC-based deployment.' For remote driving specifically, what does MEC provide that cloud cannot?

options.A: MEC provides more storage for remote driving logs
options.B: Remote driving requires <10ms control loop latency ² cloud round-trip is 50-300ms, making the vehicle unresponsive to operator control. MEC processes vehicle sensor data and control commands locally, achieving sub-10ms round trips
options.C: MEC provides higher resolution camera feeds
options.D: MEC is needed because remote driving requires IPv6 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Sidelink positioning improves localization in GNSS-challenged environments. What GNSS limitation specifically motivates this?

options.A: GNSS cannot operate above 100 km/h
options.B: Urban canyon environments (tall buildings) and tunnels block satellite signals, causing GNSS position errors of 10-50m ² sidelink ranging between nearby vehicles provides sub-meter relative positioning that complements degraded GNSS
options.C: GNSS has insufficient update rate for vehicular use
options.D: GNSS cannot function in the 5.9 GHz band 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: The final C-V2X deployment roadmap phase ('Full IoV') integrates V2X with IoT. What specific capability does IoT integration add that pure V2X cannot provide?

options.A: IoT provides higher bandwidth than V2X
options.B: IoT integration connects vehicles to non-vehicle infrastructure data ² traffic sensors, environmental monitors, smart traffic lights, pedestrian detection systems ² creating situational awareness from data sources beyond vehicles and RSUs alone
options.C: IoT replaces SCMS for certificate management
options.D: IoT provides higher security than V2X 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'MEC deployment primarily supports autonomous driving and smart mobility.' What specific real-time analytics function does MEC perform that enables autonomous driving support?

options.A: MEC stores maps for offline autonomous driving
options.B: MEC aggregates V2X data from multiple vehicles/sensors in real-time to generate a collective environmental model (birds-eye view, pedestrian tracking, intersection state), then distributes this enhanced perception to all participating vehicles
options.C: MEC controls vehicle actuators directly
options.D: MEC monitors vehicle software for security threats 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: In the V2X deployment context, what does 'backward compatibility' between LTE-V2X and NR-V2X specifically require?

options.A: NR-V2X vehicles must use LTE hardware
options.B: NR-V2X vehicles must be able to communicate with LTE-V2X vehicles using common message formats and compatible PC5 interface modes ² ensuring safety-critical V2V communication works regardless of whether a neighboring vehicle supports LTE or NR sidelink
options.C: LTE-V2X must be disabled when NR-V2X is available
options.D: Backward compatibility only applies to Uu, not PC5 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: An RSU 'collects local road data and forwards it to nearby edge computing resources.' What is the technical difference between 'co-located' MEC (at RSU) vs 'nearby' MEC (at base station)?

options.A: Co-located MEC is more expensive
options.B: Co-located MEC at the RSU eliminates backhaul latency between RSU and MEC ² data processing occurs at the point of collection. Nearby MEC at the base station adds backhaul delay (typically 1-5ms) but benefits from more powerful shared infrastructure
options.C: Co-located MEC cannot process video data
options.D: RSU-co-located MEC and base-station MEC have identical performance 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'No infrastructure dependency' is listed as a key benefit of sidelink-based positioning. In what emergency scenario is this benefit most critical?

options.A: During rush hour traffic congestion
options.B: After a natural disaster or infrastructure failure that destroys RSUs and GPS ground station infrastructure ² vehicles can still determine relative positions to each other using PC5 sidelink ranging, enabling coordinated emergency response and safe maneuvering
options.C: When OBU battery is low
options.D: When cellular coverage is at maximum capacity 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: A Sybil attack in V2X creates multiple fake identities. Why is this attack specifically dangerous for safety applications?

options.A: Sybil attacks drain vehicle batteries
options.B: Fake vehicle identities can generate false sensor data suggesting phantom traffic congestion, accidents, or road blockages ² causing real vehicles to make dangerous maneuvers or emergency stops based on non-existent hazards
options.C: Sybil attacks only affect infotainment systems
options.D: Sybil attackers can read encrypted V2X messages 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Pseudonym certificates change frequently. What specific cryptographic property prevents an adversary from linking old and new pseudonyms?

options.A: Pseudonyms use the same private key but different public keys
options.B: Each pseudonym uses a completely independent key pair (private/public) with no mathematical relationship ² proving the same vehicle owns two pseudonyms requires breaking cryptographic assumptions, not just observing message patterns
options.C: SCMS keeps pseudonym changes secret
options.D: Pseudonym changes are masked by encrypting the vehicle's real IP address 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Forward secrecy' protects past communications if a key is compromised. In a shared group key scenario (e.g., platoon), why is forward secrecy especially critical?

options.A: Forward secrecy is less important for groups than individuals
options.B: In a group with a shared key, if the key is compromised, ALL past group communications are exposed simultaneously ² without forward secrecy, one compromised vehicle retroactively reveals the entire platoon's communication history
options.C: Forward secrecy only protects against replay attacks
options.D: Group keys are always short-lived, providing inherent forward secrecy 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: CRLs (Certificate Revocation Lists) are distributed to invalidate compromised certificates. What V2X- specific challenge makes CRL distribution especially difficult?

options.A: Vehicles cannot store CRL data
options.B: CRLs must reach millions of vehicles in real-time or near-real-time ² a revoked certificate is useless if vehicles haven't received the update, but distributing large CRLs to all vehicles over V2X bandwidth is a significant scalability challenge
options.C: CRLs are only needed for RSUs, not vehicles
options.D: Regulatory rules prevent CRL distribution in some countries 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: A wormhole attack makes far vehicles appear close. Why is this attack specifically dangerous for cooperative driving applications?

options.A: Wormhole attacks consume vehicle battery
options.B: Cooperative driving decisions (e.g., whether to yield to a vehicle) depend on believing neighbors are physically nearby ² a wormhole makes a distant vehicle appear adjacent, causing vehicles to yield to or coordinate with vehicles they will never physically encounter
options.C: Wormhole attacks only affect GPS accuracy
options.D: Wormhole attackers can modify message content 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: V2X uses public key cryptography for authentication. What specific challenge of PKI does the V2X environment create that traditional internet PKI does not face?

options.A: Vehicles cannot store private keys
options.B: V2X requires verifying hundreds of BSMs per second from hundreds of vehicles simultaneously ² the computational overhead of full PKI verification at this rate strains OBU processors, requiring optimized batch verification or implicit certificates
options.C: PKI cannot work with DSRC
options.D: Public keys cannot be transmitted in DSRC BSMs 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: SCMS distributes pseudonym certificates with limited lifetime. Why is 'limited lifetime' specifically important beyond just privacy?

options.A: Limited lifetime reduces SCMS storage requirements
options.B: Short-lived certificates limit the window of opportunity for a compromised certificate to be used ² if a vehicle is compromised, its certificates expire quickly, reducing the damage an attacker can cause using stolen credentials
options.C: Certificate lifetime is determined by vehicle speed
options.D: Limited lifetime certificates use less computational resources 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Non-repudiation' via digital signatures means a sender cannot deny sending a message. Why must V2X non-repudiation be balanced against privacy?

options.A: Non-repudiation requires exposing the vehicle's permanent identity, which conflicts directly with privacy requirements ² pseudonym systems weaken non-repudiation for regular communication while SCMS preserves accountability for misbehavior investigations by authorities only
options.B: Non-repudiation makes V2X messages larger
options.C: Non-repudiation requires cellular connectivity
options.D: Non-repudiation only applies to RSU messages, not vehicle BSMs 6 Correct Answer: A

questions.question: A DoS attack floods the V2X network. How does this differ from a jamming attack in terms of attacker capability required?

options.A: DoS requires less sophisticated equipment than jamming
options.B: Jamming requires only a radio transmitter capable of flooding the 5.9 GHz band with noise ² available cheaply. DoS via message flooding requires a valid V2X certificate (or many Sybil identities) to inject authenticated messages at high rate ² higher cryptographic access is needed
options.C: Both attacks require identical attacker capabilities
options.D: DoS attacks are only possible via the internet, not radio 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Linkability of vehicle messages' is a privacy concern. What specific information in V2X messages enables linkability even without knowing the real identity?

options.A: Vehicle speed changes over time
options.B: Consistent pseudonyms used across many messages allow observers to track vehicle movement patterns ² even without knowing the real identity, location history and behavior patterns reveal private information about the driver
options.C: Encryption certificates link messages automatically
options.D: Linkability is only possible if the attacker knows the vehicle's MAC address 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: MITM attack in V2X compromises 'message authenticity and confidentiality.' In DSRC broadcast mode, which of these two properties is harder to violate?

options.A: Authenticity is harder to violate
options.B: Confidentiality ² DSRC BSMs are not encrypted (confidentiality is not required for safety broadcasts), making eavesdropping trivial. Authenticity is protected by digital signatures, making modification detectable (though not impossible for resource-rich adversaries)
options.C: Both are equally easy to violate
options.D: Neither can be violated in DSRC due to physical layer security 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: The SCMS 'handles misbehaving nodes by revoking certificates.' What is the specific technical process after misbehavior is detected?

options.A: The SCMS disables the vehicle's OBU remotely
options.B: The SCMS adds the vehicle's pseudonym certificates to the CRL, which is distributed to all V2X participants ² subsequent messages from revoked certificates are rejected by receiving vehicles after they update their CRL
options.C: The SCMS notifies law enforcement automatically
options.D: Certificate revocation stops the vehicle from driving 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Dynamic key distribution and revocation in real time' is the main challenge in V2X key management. What specific property of V2X makes traditional PKI key management insufficient?

options.A: V2X uses more certificates than other systems
options.B: Traditional PKI manages certificates for relatively static users (websites, users) ² V2X must manage millions of rapidly changing pseudonym certificates for fast-moving vehicles while distributing revocation information quickly enough to prevent compromised certificates from being used
options.C: V2X security requirements are less strict than internet security
options.D: Traditional PKI is too expensive for V2X deployment 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Message authentication 'confirms sender identity' ² but in V2X with pseudonyms, what identity is actually being confirmed?

options.A: The vehicle's license plate identity
options.B: The pseudonym identity ² authentication confirms the message was created by the holder of the private key corresponding to the pseudonym certificate, NOT the real-world vehicle identity. Real identity is hidden and only revealable by SCMS for misbehavior investigations
options.C: The driver's identity via biometric certificate
options.D: The vehicle's insurance and registration identity 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: A V2X attacker 'modifies a legitimate message' ² which security property is violated and why does the receiver detect this?

options.A: Confidentiality is violated, detected by decryption failure
options.B: Integrity is violated ² the message's digital signature is computed over the original content using the sender's private key; any modification of message bits causes the signature verification (using the public key) to fail, indicating tampering
options.C: Availability is violated, detected by timeout
options.D: Authentication is violated, detected by certificate mismatch 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Short-lived certificates enhance pseudonymity.' What specific tracking resistance does short lifetime provide that a long-lived pseudonym does not?

options.A: Short-lived certificates use shorter encryption keys
options.B: A long-lived pseudonym used repeatedly over weeks creates a trackable profile ² observing the same pseudonym at location A and B allows trajectory reconstruction. Short-lived certificates changed frequently limit the temporal window a single pseudonym can be observed, fragmenting tracking attempts
options.C: Short-lived certificates cannot be added to CRLs
options.D: Long-lived pseudonyms are prohibited by 3GPP standards 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Latency is a security concern in V2X' because delays undermine timely threat response. What specific scenario demonstrates this?

options.A: An OBU that processes certificates slowly
options.B: A revocation notice reaching a vehicle 500ms after a misbehaving neighbor transmits a hazard spoofing message ² the victim vehicle has already acted on the false data before the revocation arrives, illustrating how latency in security infrastructure enables attacks
options.C: A cellular network with high ping time
options.D: An RSU that validates certificates slowly 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Jamming attacks 'isolate vehicles from the V2X network.' Against what type of V2X safety application is jamming MOST dangerous?

options.A: Navigation and mapping applications
options.B: Event-driven safety alerts (emergency braking, collision warnings) ² these are non-periodic and critical; a vehicle being jammed at the exact moment it needs to receive an emergency alert misses the only warning with potentially fatal consequences
options.C: Weather updates and traffic information
options.D: Over-the-air software update applications 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: Asymmetric cryptography (public/private key) is chosen over symmetric for V2X authentication. What specific V2X operational requirement makes symmetric key approaches unscalable?

options.A: Symmetric keys are easier to intercept over radio
options.B: Symmetric authentication requires the verifier to share a secret key with every possible sender ² in V2X, a vehicle must authenticate BSMs from any of millions of unknown nearby vehicles, requiring millions of pre-shared keys. Asymmetric keys allow authentication from any vehicle whose certificate is signed by a trusted CA
options.C: Symmetric encryption is not supported by DSRC hardware
options.D: SCMS cannot distribute symmetric keys 6 Correct Answer: B

questions.question: 'Providing scalable certificate distribution and revocation' is SCMS's key motivation. What scale specifically must SCMS handle?

options.A: Thousands of certificates per city
options.B: Hundreds of millions of pseudonym certificates for tens of millions of vehicles, each using multiple short-lived pseudonyms simultaneously ² plus real-time revocation distribution to all active vehicles globally. No traditional PKI was designed for this scale
options.C: Certificate distribution only for RSUs and TMCs
options.D: SCMS only handles certificates for emergency vehicles 6 Correct Answer: B
